newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ monetary conditions tight in October - BTNZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ monetary conditions tight in October - BTNZ.

text.p: An analysis of monetary conditions by Bankers Trust released on Monday has confirmed that conditions in October were much tighter than the Reserve Bank was projecting.

Bankers Trust said the average reading of its monetary conditions index in October was 137, up from the September average of 133.5. This was higher than the 126 index level implied by Reserve Bank projections for the December quarter.
The index combines the 90-day bank bill rate and the trade weighted currency index to produce an overall measure of monetary conditions.
It was above the Reserve Bank's assumed comfort zone for most of October, dipping near the end of the month after the central bank said that conditions were tighter than needed.
Bankers Trust economist David Plank said the rising currency was the main reason conditions were tighter than projected. The Kiwi dollar traded at eight and a half year highs during October.
"The RBNZ (Reserve Bank) has had to accept lower interest rates and a higher exchange rate than it would ideally like," he said.
Plank said private sector wages data due later this month and fiscal policy were likely to hold the key to future easing of policy.
The Reserve Bank is due to release its monetary policy statement on December 17.
